3. Since both aforesaid appeals are arising out of the common award dated 02.11.2015 passed by Third MACT, Gwalior in common Claim Case No.372 of 2014, therefore, they are heard analogously and disposed of by this common order.

4. As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of deceased Bhagwan Singh, an amount of compensation in M.A.No.138/2016 to the tune of Rs.4,05,000/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal in favour of claimants with interest from filing of claim petition till its realization.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the claimants in M.A.No.138/2016 submitted that the compensation awarded by Claims Tribunal is on lower side.

It is further submitted that deceased was working at the time of accident as skilled labour by doing work of Mason and used to earn Rs.15,000/- per month, but Claims Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of deceased at Rs.4,000/- per month which is on lower side.
It is further submitted that Claims Tribunal has also wrongly applied multiplier because age of deceased was below than 60 years and Tribunal has assessed age of the deceased as 68 years.
The further contention of appellant that Claims Tribunal has also erred in not awarding reasonable amount in other heads i.e. loss of estate, loss of consortium, funeral expenses etc.
Hence, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24964 3 MA-107-2016 prayed for setting aside the impugned award and seeking enhancement of compensation.

6. Learned counsel appearing for owner and driver of the offending vehicle in M.A.No.107/2016 submitted that at the time of accident, vehicle was going for repairing for which no route permit was needed.
So, Claims Tribunal has wrongly recorded a finding that it is a breach of terms and conditions of Insurance Policy.
Hence, it is prayed that first liability lies upon the Insurance Company to pay compensation in favour of claimants jointly and severally with owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
7. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company supported the impugned award passed in both claim cases and prayed for rejection of the both the appeals.

8. Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the entire record.
9.

So far as the contention of counsel for the owner and driver of the offending vehicle that at the time of accident, vehicle was sent for repairing work for which no need of route permit is concerned,
owner and driver of the offending vehicle were unable to adduce any substantial document/evidence to prove that alleged vehicle was sent to service centre for service.
On perusal of written statements filed by owner and driver of the offending vehicle, it is clear that this fact was also not mentioned there that the vehicle was sent for service to service centre.

Therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, owner and driver of the offending vehicle were unable to prove that at the time of accident, vehicle was coming from the service centre after NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24964 4 MA-107-2016 its service.

So, Claims Tribunal has rightly held that owner and driver of the offending vehicle have breached the terms and conditions of the Insurance Smt. Malti @ Mahanto vs Mukesh Kumar Rawat on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133995891/
2 Policy.

sentences.text: Since deceased was a third party, therefore, Claims Tribunal has rightly recorded a finding that Insurance Company is liable to firstly pay compensation amount in favour of claimants with liberty to recover the same from owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
So, finding recorded in this regard by Claims Tribunal is just and proper.
Thus, no need of interference of this Court in this regard is required.

10. The next contention of learned counsel for claimants that deceased was working as Mason and he used to earn Rs.15,000/- per month, but the Claims Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of deceased as Rs.4000/- per month.
Claims Tribunal ought to have assessed the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act of unskilled labour.

11. On perusal of the record, it is found that although deceased was unable to adduce any substantial document/evidence in regard to prove the income of the deceased and was also unable to prove the fact that deceased was a skilled labour.

12. So far as the contention of claimants with regard to age of the deceased below 60 years is concerned, according to the document (Voter List) produced by claimants before the Claims Tribunal, the age of the deceased was 68 years at the time of accident, therefore, finding recorded by Claims Tribunal in this regard needs no interference of this Court.
There are seven claimants in M.A.No.138/2016 in which, Claimant No.1 is wife of deceased and claimants No.2 to 7 are children of deceased.
Therefore, they NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24964 5 MA-107-2016 are dependent on the income of the deceased.
Thus, the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in only deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses in stead of 1/5th.

So, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, Claims Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of 5.

Income  annum  Dependency Rs.56112/-
 Loss of Income Rs.280560/-

sentences.text: Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in M.A.No.138/2016 is Rs.5,90,560/- as against the Award of the Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24964 6 MA-107-2016 Tribunal of Rs.4,05,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,85,560/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
15. In the result, this M.A.No.138/2016 is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,85,560/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

16. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
17. In view of the above, M.A.No.138/2016 filed by the claimants is partly allowed and M.A.No.107/2016 is dismissed.
Let a copy of this order be placed in MA No.138/2016.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
